Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, Planning Commission Members will be participating via
teleconference.

- Commission meeting videos are live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city/agendas and available for
viewing thereafter.

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone, Meeting ID:
836 5409 3351, Meeting Password: 512700. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using the call-in
option from a phone line.)

-  Public  correspondence  may  be  emailed  to  Carol Corea, Administrative  Assistant  at
carolc@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the meeting will be forwarded to
the Commission for their consideration and included as part of the record.

- Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos”
page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/agendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment”
button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After
you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
public, will be considered by the Commission and become part of the record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting, may join by visiting http://www.zoom.com/join
and enter the following credentials: Meeting ID: 836 5409 3351, Meeting Password: 512700.

- If using a tablet or phone, download the Zoom app and enter the following credentials: Meeting ID: 836 5409
3351, Meeting Password: 512700.

Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the agenda you
would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each agenda item are available on the City's
website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city/agendas.

MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, AUGUST 3, 2020

  A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
  order by CHAIR CARMAN at 7:00 p.m. Pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20, this
  meeting was held via teleconference.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR CARMAN led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioner’s Present:  Carman, Edler, Medawar, Schachter, Scott, Yoo, Zigrang

  Staff Member’s Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES, JULY 6, 2020

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF JULY 6, 2020.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CARMAN so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A.  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to the Planning
  Commission will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read by title only.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6A

  There being no objection, CHAIR CARMAN so ordered.

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-20-18 (MODIFICATION); LOCATION: 19
  DAPPLEGRAY LANE; APPLICANT: MS. SHEELA DERANIYAGALA; A request to Modify
  approvals granted by the Planning Commission on March 4, 2019, which included a
  Neighborhood Compatibility Determination for a one-story addition and deck to an existing
  one-story, single family residence; a Minor Deviation for the one-story addition to be built
  along the existing building line that encroaches into the legal nonconforming sideyard
  setback; and a Grading Permit for removal of the existing tennis court and related facilities.
  The applicant requests to modify the Minor Deviation approval with a four (4) foot extension
PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  1
MINUTES, August 3, 2020
   of the rear covered deck, which would maintain a 4’-11” nonconforming sideyard setback,
  and modification of the Grading Permit approval, by reduction of the grading involved with
  the tennis court and related facilities removal.

  Planning Manager Naughton provided a presentation on Planning Application No. PA-20-18, a
  request for a modification to entitlements which were approved on March 4, 2019. The original
  entitlements were for a Minor Deviation for a one story addition to be built along the existing building
  line that encroaches into the legal nonconforming side yard setback and a Grading Permit for the
  removal of the existing tennis court and related facilities.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that from the original plan the deck includes an additional 4-
  foot extension and the relocation of the stairs off the deck. The original grading plan included
  removing the tennis court, retaining wall and all related facilities, which would involve 192 cubic
  yards of material to be removed and 6 cubic yards of fill. The project would have brought down the
  grade significantly and added a 24-inch curb along the southern property line. The property owners
  were not approved by the Homeowners Association to utilize the bridle trail to bring in any earth
  moving equipment or construction vehicles. The original grading plan became infeasible.

  The applicants constructed the 4-foot extension without obtaining permits and a stop work order
  was issued for the deck.

  There is a concern from the neighbor at 21 Dapplegray Lane with privacy concerns due to the
  additional 4-foot extension. The idea of putting up a privacy screen or live wall was discussed and
  these would provide reasonable privacy for both parties.

  The owners at property address, 17 Dapplegray Lane are also concerned with privacy once the
  tennis court is removed. One of the options is to put a 6-foot wall in front of the retaining wall, which
  would eliminate a garden area and would not really resolve the privacy concern; the second option
  would be to put a fence behind the retaining wall, which would cause 19 Dapplegray to lose 10-
  feet of their property. The applicants may voluntarily apply for a variance in order to construct a 6-
  foot fence on top of the retaining wall.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff is able to support the project, subject to the conditions
  outlined in the staff report.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACTHER asked how the 3805 sq. ft. of the tennis court will be removed.
  Planning Manager Naughton stated that they will need to remove it manually and remove the
  material through the less than 5 ft. side yard.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked why the entire tennis court will not be removed. Planning
  Manager Naughton stated that it is a cost issue.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked if staff had ever reviewed plans for the larger deck. Planning
  Manager Naughton stated that staff was alerted of the larger deck from a complaint that was
  received.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked if any work was done after the stop work was given. Planning
  Manger Naughton stated that the roof and covering was done after the stop work was given.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG expressed his concern regarding why the additional 4 ft. was not
  caught when the building department signed off on the foundation.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  2
MINUTES, August 3, 2020
   COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER inquired why the HOA denied the application to use the bridle
  trail. Planning Manager Naughton stated that the HOA denied the applicant’s request to use the
  bridle trail to be used for construction activity.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked if the other privacy issues mentioned in the staff report are
  being addressed. Planning Manger Naughton stated that the other privacy issues are having to do
  with 17 Dapplegray Lane and would require the applicant to voluntarily apply for a variance to
  address those concerns.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked if the privacy issue is any worse on the southerly side if the tennis
  court is removed. Planning Manager Naughton stated that a chain link fence would not provide
  much privacy.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked if an option to do a solid wall was discussed at the edge of the deck.
  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the applicant preferred the live wall option.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked if the neighbor at 21 Dapplegray had a preference in privacy
  options. Planning Manager Naughton stated she has not discussed the preferred privacy option
  with the owner of 21 Dapplegray.

  Sam Silva, representing19 Dapplegray, stated that the building inspector did not have a problem
  with the deck extension, but they failed to resubmit revised plans to planning. At the time of
  construction, the deck was quite small and the deck was extended. Regarding the concrete removal
  of the tennis court, the designers had charged a large sum to come up with a design to remove the
  concrete and tennis court. This would have created a slope in their yard that would be unusable.
  Mr. Silva came up with a design to maintain some of the concrete and utilize it for walkways and
  patio areas.

  Sheela Deraniyagala, 19 Dapplegray Lane, stated that at the time she purchased the home, she
  was not aware that the tennis court was non-conforming and stated that staff told her that the tennis
  court needed to be removed. Ms. Deraniyagala stated that she does not want to disturb the trees
  on the side of 17 Dapplegray Lane. In regards to 21 Dapplegray Lane, she stated that there are
  privacy issues whether or not the deck is extended. Ms. Deraniyagala stated that this property has
  had ongoing expenses since May 2018 when she acquired the property. She would like to support
  her neighbors and have the support of her neighbors.

  Grant Mogford, 21 Dapplegray Lane, expressed his concerns with privacy issues due to the
  additional 4 ft. extension. He stated lowering the deck or taking the deck back to the original plan
  would be solutions.

  Gary Johnson, 17 Dapplegray Lane, stated that he is not opposed to the project and agreed that
  the best thing to do is to put the 6 ft. fence on top of the retaining wall.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCOTT, Mr. Silva explained that the choice to
  maintain the portion of concrete closest to 17 Dapplegray Lane has to do with the amount of
  concrete that would have to be removed. The area that is being proposed to be removed is the
  thinnest portion.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCOTT, Planning Manager Naughton stated that
  staff would be willing to support a variance, but it would be difficult to make the findings.

  Further discussion ensued.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  3
MINUTES, August 3, 2020
   In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCOTT, Mr. Mogford stated that his preference
  would be to have the applicant construct a 33 ft. solid wall along the northerly side of the deck and
  at the corner post turn towards that south.

  Ms. Deraniyagala expressed her concern since originally when the plans were approved there were
  no issues and stated that she could install a 4 ft. solid wall on the portion that was extended.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG suggested a 6 ft. solid wall on along the deck to provide privacy.
  Otherwise, he would recommend taking the deck back to the original design.

  A discussion ensued regarding the wall along the deck.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER expressed his concern how this issue developed.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR expressed his concern with moving forward with this project and to
  make sure that it is being constructed to plan.

  COMMISSIONER EDLER stated that he is not ready to approve this modification.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT commented that a variance may resolve the privacy issue with the
  neighbor at 17 Dapplegray. He also expressed his dissatisfaction with the explanation provided
  regarding building the extension without prior approval.

  CHAIR CARMAN agreed that the privacy of the neighbor is compromised by the extension of the
  unpermitted deck. She stated that a solid wall should be constructed or the deck should be built
  according to the original plan.

  The Commissioners agreed that a variance for the 6 ft. wall above the retaining wall would be an
  acceptable solution.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  CONTINUE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-20-18 TO A DATE UNCERTAIN TO GIVE
  THE APPLICANT TIME TO RESOLVE THE PRIVACY ISSUES WITH BOTH NEIGHBORS
  AND COME BACK WITH AGREED UPON SOLUTION.

  Ayes: Carman, Edler, Medawar, Schachter, Scott, Yoo, Zigrang
  Noes:
  Absent:
  Abstain:

  8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  NONE

  9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked for status on the house on Lantana. Planning Manager Naughton
  stated they have active permits and there has been movement in getting revised plans. Code
  Compliance has been going out to make sure that the site is secure and no debris or trash has been
  found and seems to be well maintained. Code Compliance makes visits to the site every week.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  4
MINUTES, August 3, 2020
   10.  PLANNING MANAGER ITEMS

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the next Planning Commission meeting conflicts with the
  City Council meeting in September and asked if the Commissioners are available for a special
  meeting on Monday, August 31, 2020. The Commissioners agreed that they are available.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that MBI will be drafting the ADU program and should be ready
  to present to the commission in early Fall.

  11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  PARK AND ACITIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES, JULY 20, 2020

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEMS 11A

  There being no objection, CHAIR CARMAN so ordered.

  10.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR CARMAN adjourned the meeting at 8:25 pm to the next Special Planning Commission
  meeting on Monday, August 31, 2020 at 7:00 p.m., which will be held by Video Teleconference.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant  Bridget Carman, Chair

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  5
MINUTES, August 3, 2020
